items.text: To address this limitation, we introduce the Longformer with an attention mechanism that scales linearly with sequence length, making it easy to process documents of thousands of tokens or longer.
items.why: Introduces Longformer and its linear scaling mechanism.
items.plain: We introduce Longformer, which uses an attention mechanism that scales linearly with sequence length so it can process documents with thousands of tokens or more.

items.text: Following prior work on long-sequence transformers, we evaluate Longformer on character-level language modeling and achieve state-of-the-art results on text8 and enwik8.
items.why: State-of-the-art results on language modeling benchmarks.
items.plain: We evaluate Longformer on character-level language modeling and get state-of-the-art results on the text8 and enwik8 datasets.

items.text: Our pretrained Longformer consistently outperforms RoBERTa on long document tasks and sets new state-of-the-art results on Wiki- Hop and TriviaQA.
items.why: Headline result on downstream long-document tasks.
items.plain: Our pretrained Longformer consistently outperforms RoBERTa on long document tasks and sets new state-of-the-art results on Wiki-Hop and TriviaQA.

items.text: We ﬁnally introduce the Longformer-Encoder-Decoder (LED), a Longformer variant for supporting long document generative sequence-to-sequence tasks, and demonstrate its effectiveness on the arXiv summarization dataset.1
items.why: Introduces the sequence-to-sequence variant of Longformer.
items.plain: We introduce the Longformer-Encoder-Decoder (LED) for long document generative sequence-to-sequence tasks and show that it works well on the arXiv summarization dataset.

items.why: States the core problem with standard Transformers.
items.plain: Standard self-attention memory and computation grow quadratically with sequence length, making it infeasible or very expensive to process long sequences.

items.text: Longformer’s attention mechanism is a combination of a windowed local-context self-attention and an end task motivated global attention that encodes inductive bias about the task.
items.why: Explains the two core attention components.
items.plain: Longformer combines a windowed local-context self-attention with a global attention designed for the specific end task.

items.text: Through ablations and controlled trials we show both attention types are essential – the local attention is primarily used to build contextual representations, while the global attention allows Longformer to build full sequence representations for prediction.
items.why: States the functional roles of local versus global attention.
items.plain: Local attention builds contextual representations, while global attention lets the model build full-sequence representations for prediction.

items.text: We achieve a new state-of-the-art on both text8 and enwik8 using the small models with BPC of 1.10 and 1.00 on text8 and enwik8 respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of our model.
items.why: Headline result numbers for small character-level models.
items.plain: We achieve a new state-of-the-art on text8 and enwik8 using small models, achieving BPC scores of 1.10 on text8 and 1.00 on enwik8.

items.text: We observe that Longformer consistently outperforms the RoBERTa baseline.
items.why: Core claim regarding fine-tuning across tasks.
items.plain: Longformer consistently outperforms the RoBERTa baseline across all fine-tuning tasks.

items.text: Tab. 8 shows that our Longformer-large achieves new state-of-the-art results9 on WikiHop and TriviaQA by large margins (3.6 and 4 points respectively), and for HotpotQA, it underperforms the current state-of-the-art (Fang et al., 2020) by a point.
items.why: Headline state-of-the-art results on QA datasets.
items.plain: Longformer-large achieves new state-of-the-art results on WikiHop and TriviaQA by 3.6 and 4 points, while slightly underperforming the state-of-the-art on HotpotQA by one point.

items.text: We call this model Longformer-Encoder-Decoder (LED) which scales linearly with the input.
items.why: Defines LED and its computational scaling.
items.plain: We call this model the Longformer-Encoder-Decoder (LED), which scales linearly with the input length.

items.text: We observe that LED achieves stateof-the-art results on arXiv, slightly outperforming BigBird (Zaheer et al., 2020).
items.why: Headline result for the LED model on summarization.
items.plain: LED achieves state-of-the-art results on the arXiv summarization dataset, slightly outperforming BigBird.

items.text: Fig. 3 further illustrates the importance of sequence length showing the ablility to process longer input signiﬁcantly improves the results.
items.why: Key takeaway on input length for summarization performance.
items.plain: Being able to process longer inputs significantly improves the model's summarization results.

items.text: We present Longformer, a transformer-based model
items.why: Introduces Longformer as a scalable document-processing transformer model.
items.plain: We introduce Longformer, a transformer model designed for natural language processing.

items.text: that is scalable for processing long documents and that makes it easy to perform a wide range of document-level NLP tasks without chunking/shortening the long input and without complex architecture to combine information across these chunks.
items.why: Explains Longformer's ability to process long documents without chunking.
items.plain: It processes long documents easily without needing to shorten them, break them into chunks, or use complex architectures to combine information.

items.text: Longformer employs an attention pattern that combines local and global information while also scaling linearly with the sequence length.
items.why: Describes the core attention mechanism scaling linearly with length.
items.plain: It uses an attention pattern that combines local and global context while its computation grows linearly with input length.

items.text: Longformer achieves state-of-the-art results on the character-level language modeling tasks of text8

items.plain: Longformer achieves state-of-the-art results on text8 character-level language modeling tasks.

items.text: When pretrained, Longformer consistently outperforms RoBERTa on long document tasks and sets new state-of-the-art results on WikiHop and TriviaQA.
items.why: Presents key performance gains over RoBERTa and state-of-the-art results.
items.plain: When pretrained, Longformer consistently beats RoBERTa on long document tasks and sets new state-of-the-art performance on WikiHop and TriviaQA.

items.text: We further present LED, an encoder-decoder variant of Longformer for modeling sequence-to-sequence tasks, and achieve stateof-the-art results on the arXiv long document summarization task.
items.why: Introduces LED variant and state-of-the-art summarization results.
items.plain: We also present LED, an encoder-decoder version of Longformer for sequence-to-sequence tasks, which achieves state-of-the-art results on the arXiv long document summarization benchmark.
